Hyper-realistic cinematic shot of a supermassive black hole in deep space, in the visual style of the black hole Gargantua from the film Interstellar, but with an icy blue color palette instead of orange. A perfectly black event horizon sits at the center of the frame, surrounded by a thin, intensely bright photon ring of white-blue light. A glowing accretion disk of swirling plasma in cool blue, cyan and pale white tones wraps around it; gravitational lensing bends the far side of the disk up and over the top and under the bottom of the black hole, creating the iconic halo shape. The plasma in the disk flows slowly and continuously in a circular orbit, with fine turbulent filaments and subtle brightness variations. The near side of the disk is brighter (relativistic Doppler beaming). Faint, sparse distant stars in a near-black background with a very subtle deep navy tint, slightly warped by lensing near the edges of the black hole.

Static locked-off camera, no camera movement, no zoom. Extremely slow, calm, hypnotic motion. Seamless, steady, continuous rotation of the accretion disk. Symmetrical centered composition with plenty of dark negative space around the black hole. Photorealistic, IMAX film grain, anamorphic cinematic look, high dynamic range, soft bloom on the brightest parts, deep true blacks, subtle volumetric glow. 8K detail, scientifically accurate, Kip Thorne black hole visualization.

A single uninterrupted shot for a looping desktop background. Maintain the exact same framing, event-horizon position and scale throughout. The event horizon occupies roughly one fifth of the frame width, with luminous lensed plasma above and below. Restrained blue-white highlights and true black negative space. No text, no logos, no spacecraft, no planets, no visible UI. Silent footage.
